Figure 1:Overview of FactEmbed.Given a composed query and a target image, FactEmbed introduces a compact set of learnable factorized latents into the input sequence.
To enforce structured factorization without requiring dense annotations, we attach a decoder to an intermediate MLLM layer, which utilizes these latents as an information bottleneck to reconstruct target patch features via a target imagination objective.
In addition, we apply a factor-level InfoNCE to the resulting latents{uk}k=1K\{u_{k}\}_{k=1}^{K}to leverage the decomposed factors for retrieval, while global-level embeddingzzis trained with the instance-level InfoNCE objective.

Figure 3:Qualitative analysis of target imagination.For each composed query, we visualize target DINOv2 features (DINOv2 PCA) and features imagined by our decoder from the query (Recon PCA), projected onto a joint PCA basis.
Alpha Mask Argmax shows, for each spatial positionpp, the factorized latent with the largest decoder alpha weight,i.e.,arg⁡maxk⁡ℳ¯k,p\arg\max_{k}\bar{\mathcal{M}}_{k,p}, where each color denotes a different latent.
On top of the coarse layout from the target prior, fine details are recovered by the latents, jointly reconstructing the target structure.

Figure 4:Impact of layout prior in target imagination.Three rows compare factor decomposition across different layout prior configurations: (top) without a layout prior, (middle) with a1×11\times 1layout prior, and (bottom) with our default2×22\times 2layout prior.
While the unconditioned model collapses into coarse global semantics, introducing the2×22\times 2layout prior guides the latents to isolate semantically editable parts.
